## Intuition

A **Markov process** is a stochastic process indexed by time whose future is
independent of its past given the present, the **Markov property**. Markov
processes describe memoryless real-world systems that evolve based only on
their current state.

The general (and strong) Markov property is stated in [[markov-property]]. The
discrete-time, countable-state case is developed in [[markov-chains]] and its
sub-topics; this note concerns the general picture and continuous time.

## Classification

Markov processes fall into four groups according to the time index and the
state space:

| | Countable state space | General state space |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Discrete time** | [[markov-chains]] | Markov chains on a measurable state space |
| **Continuous time** | [[jump-processes]] | diffusions and other processes, e.g. [[brownian-motion]] |

## Transition semigroup

For a time-homogeneous process on a state space $S$ the **transition
function** is $P_{t}(x,A)=\mathbb{P}(X_{t+s}\in A|X_{s}=x)$. The Markov
property implies the [[chapman-kolmogorov-equations|Chapman-Kolmogorov
equations]]
$$
P_{t+s}(x,A)=\int_{S}P_{s}(x,dy)\,P_{t}(y,A),
$$
so that $(P_{t})_{t\geq0}$ is a semigroup of operators acting on functions by
$P_{t}f(x)=\mathbb{E}[f(X_{t})|X_{0}=x]$. Differentiating this semigroup at
$t=0$ gives the [[infinitesimal-generator]], and the evolution of
$P_{t}$ and of the law of $X_{t}$ is described by the
[[kolmogorov-equations]] (backward and forward).
